sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Aí is an Irish god. This minor divinity was a poet of the magical race of Ireland, the Tuatha Dé Danann. At his birth a prophet predicted that he would wield great power. This prediction alarmed a king. The king tried to murder the infant. Aí's father saved the child so that his destiny could be fulfilled. The details of that destined greatness are lost. Only the opening of the tale survives in the sources. The name Aí is also written Aoi or Aoi mac Ollamain. The title mac Ollamain links him to the office of chief poet. His story shows how the Tuatha Dé Danann guarded the fates of their young.

okr.objective: This article establishes Aí as a minor Irish god and poet of the Tuatha Dé Danann whose fated power was lost.
